newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank proposes umbrella mkt, bank watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank proposes umbrella mkt, bank watchdog.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) has submitted proposals to parliament to create an umbrella markets watchdog to boost confidence in the local financial and capital markets.

According to a CNB report to parliament obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, the proposals include creating a central supervisory body to oversee the work of regulators on the banking, insurance and capital markets, including investment funds.

"We recommend...an institutionally anchored organ for the functional cooperation of supervision, in which there would be representatives of institutions, to regulate individual segments of the financial market -- (banks, capital markets, funds, insurance, etc)," the report said.
"This (new) institution would, among other things, monitor the activities of diversified financial groups on the markets..." it added.

The 31-page report also proposes that the new organ be allowed to "make changes in the managment of funds, halt voting rights, and force the eventual sale of shares" held by entities which bring "a threatening influence" to banks and financial institutions.

The report, reviewing the forced administration of 12 Czech banks in recent years and the failure of many of them, was released by the central bank ahead of the testimony of CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky to parliament later this afternoon.

The report also calls on parliament to mandate stronger prudence on lending practices, strengthen the execution of existing regulations, and further enable the prevention of financial crime and "non-concrete" entry of investors into the capital markets.
It also calls for:
- Quarterly public statements by banks of their activities and structure
- More frequent reports by funds stating the structure of their investments
- Improvement in the capacity of commercial courts to handle cases of bankruptcy and financial crime
- Stronger use of external auditors and harmonisation of Czech accounting laws to match international accounting standards (IAS)
The Czech financial markets have been severely criticised by investors for insider trading activities and lack of transparency.

The criticism became a heated political battle after the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. in August and subsequent liquidity crisis at Agrobanka a.s. which was put under forced administration in September.

The central bank said that a crisis of confidence caused by Kreditni's and Agrobanka's connection with the secretive investment group Motoinvest made larger banks pull back on the interbank lending market and made Agrobanka illiquid.

The CNB blames the problems in recent years of many smaller banks on the difficult trading environment -- especially on the interbank market because of their low volume of deposits -- and the general transformation of the Czech economy from communism.
It said poor regulation mainly of the capital markets -- especially funds in takeover battles with banks -- can potentially weaken the financial strength of banks and lower their credibility.
That responds to allegations by Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus who put much of the blame for the banking failures on the Czech National Bank.
Capital market regulation is currently under the auspices of the Finance Ministry.
-- John Mastrini, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2-2423-0003
